name: Kommo
tagline: The 15-year-old, self-funded CRM (formerly amoCRM) that rebuilt itself around WhatsApp and Instagram messaging — genuinely differentiated as a CRM, with real documented billing and integration-reliability complaints.
tldr: Kommo has operated since 2009 under the name amoCRM before rebranding to Kommo in October 2022, is published by QSOFT LLC, and — unusually for this category — has raised no outside funding at all, operating independently with thousands of customers across 100+ countries.

This is fundamentally a sales CRM with messaging layered natively on top, not a messaging tool with CRM features bolted on — reviewers specifically describe it as 'the only CRM found that integrated with Social Media messaging' as a genuine differentiator.

Pricing is per-seat and published clearly: Base $15/user/mo, Advanced $25/user/mo (adds the Salesbot no-code chatbot builder), Pro $45/user/mo, Enterprise custom — with a minimum 6-month subscription commitment and a 14-day free trial requiring no credit card.

The Salesbot AI builder handles lead qualification and follow-up well for scripted, structured conversations, and a separate GPT-4o/GPT-4o mini-powered widget transcribes and analyzes calls — but independent analysis specifically notes Salesbot weakens when handling unstructured, open-ended dialogue.

Real, serious complaints exist beyond typical software gripes: at least one reviewer reports being automatically charged $400 without requesting renewal with no resolution from the company, and the Shopify integration is specifically described as failing weekly with support taking days to resolve issues.

Best for sales-driven teams that want messaging-native lead management inside a genuine CRM pipeline — not for teams whose priority is a fully reliable, deeply-integrated ecommerce or open-ended AI conversation experience, given the documented integration and billing concerns.
keyFeatures: A visual sales pipeline for tracking deals, native to the CRM rather than bolted on afterward
Salesbot — a no-code chatbot builder (Advanced tier and up) for automating lead qualification and follow-up conversations
A GPT-4o and GPT-4o mini-powered AI widget for transcribing and analyzing sales calls
Native centralization of WhatsApp, Instagram, email, and call conversations directly inside CRM contact records
Workflow automation for routing, tagging, and follow-up sequencing without requiring advanced technical knowledge
Mobile app access for managing leads and conversations on the go
API integrations for email, telephony, and website connectivity
A documented Shopify integration, though independent reports describe real reliability issues with it

faq.question: Is Kommo the same product as amoCRM?
faq.answer: Yes — Kommo is amoCRM rebranded in October 2022. The name change reflects the product's evolution from a traditional sales CRM into a messaging-native platform, with 'Kommo' evoking 'communicate' and the Spanish/Portuguese/French word for 'how.' There's no separate legacy product; it's a direct continuation under a new name.

faq.question: How is Kommo different from a typical WhatsApp business tool?
faq.answer: Kommo starts from CRM fundamentals — a visual sales pipeline, deal tracking, and contact management — and layers WhatsApp and Instagram messaging natively on top, rather than the reverse. Reviewers specifically describe this as a genuine differentiator: it's positioned as one of the few CRMs with truly native social-messaging integration, rather than a messaging tool with a thin CRM veneer.

faq.question: How good is Kommo's Salesbot AI?
faq.answer: It handles scripted, structured conversations — lead qualification, follow-up sequencing — well, and a separate GPT-4o-powered widget transcribes and analyzes sales calls competently. Independent analysis specifically notes, though, that Salesbot's performance weakens when handling unstructured, open-ended dialogue, so it's better suited to well-defined conversation flows than free-form customer support.

faq.question: What's the most serious complaint about Kommo?
faq.answer: Two specific, credible issues stand out beyond typical software complaints. First, at least one reviewer reports being automatically charged $400 without requesting a renewal, with the company reportedly taking no responsibility when the charge was disputed. Second, the Shopify integration is specifically described as failing on a weekly basis, with support taking days to resolve each incident — a real reliability concern for any ecommerce-dependent workflow.

faq.question: How much does Kommo actually cost?
faq.answer: Base is $15/user/month, Advanced (which adds the Salesbot builder) is $25/user/month, Pro is $45/user/month, and Enterprise is custom-priced — all billed per seat with a minimum 6-month commitment required. A 14-day free trial with no credit card required lets you test the platform before committing to that minimum term.

faq.question: Is Kommo good for ecommerce businesses on Shopify?
faq.answer: Approach with caution specifically here. While a Shopify integration exists, independent reports describe it failing on a weekly basis with slow support resolution — a real, documented reliability problem rather than a hypothetical concern. If Shopify integration is central to your use case, test this specific integration thoroughly during the trial period before committing to the 6-month minimum term.

pricingBreakdown: Kommo's per-seat pricing ($15-45/user/month) is straightforward and competitive against comparable CRM-plus-messaging tools, and the minimum 6-month commitment is at least stated upfront rather than hidden. What deserves real scrutiny, though, is a specific, credible independent report of an unauthorized $400 charge applied without a renewal request, with no resolution offered when disputed. This is a different, more serious category of concern than typical pricing complexity — it's a billing-integrity question, and worth raising directly with Kommo's sales team (and getting written confirmation of cancellation and auto-renewal terms) before committing to the required minimum term. Beyond the base subscription, factor in that basic WhatsApp functionality has been reported as locked behind paywalls in some configurations, so confirm exactly what messaging capability your chosen tier actually includes rather than assuming full WhatsApp access at every price point.

capabilities.note: This is Kommo's genuine differentiator and the reason to consider it over a messaging-first competitor: WhatsApp, Instagram, email, and call conversations land directly inside CRM contact records against a real sales pipeline, rather than a chat tool with a thin CRM layer bolted on. Reviewers specifically and repeatedly credit this as a rare combination in the category.

Genuinely useful for its intended purpose — scripted lead qualification and follow-up sequencing — but independent analysis is specific and consistent that it weakens on unstructured, open-ended conversations. Pair it with the GPT-4o call-analysis widget for a fuller picture of its actual AI capability, and don't expect it to replace a dedicated open-ended support AI.

A real, documented concern rather than a hypothetical one: the Shopify integration is specifically reported as failing on a weekly basis, with support taking days to resolve each incident. Given how central reliable ecommerce integration is to many buyers' use case, this is worth stress-testing directly during the 14-day trial before committing to the required 6-month minimum term.

Worth flagging directly given the specificity of the complaint on record: at least one reviewer describes an unauthorized $400 charge applied without a renewal request, disputed with no resolution from the company. Get explicit, written cancellation and auto-renewal terms before signing, and monitor your first billing cycle closely.

A genuine, if quiet, strength: fifteen years of continuous operation (since 2009 as amoCRM) with no outside funding raised is a real signal of sustainable, profitable operation rather than growth funded by investor capital that could run out or force a strategic pivot.

verdict: Kommo's core differentiator is real and worth taking seriously: this is one of the few products in this category that genuinely started as a CRM and built messaging natively into the pipeline, rather than the far more common pattern of a messaging tool adding a thin CRM layer afterward. Fifteen years of continuous, self-funded operation under the amoCRM name before its 2022 rebrand is a genuine signal of sustainable business health that most venture-backed competitors in this comparison set can't claim, and reviewers consistently credit the native social-messaging integration as a rare, real strength. Salesbot extends that CRM-first philosophy sensibly into AI — it's genuinely effective for scripted, structured lead-qualification flows, backed by a real GPT-4o-powered call-analysis capability, even though independent analysis is specific that it weakens on unstructured, open-ended conversations. Where I have to be direct and weigh things down meaningfully is two specific, credible complaint patterns that go beyond typical software friction: a documented account of an unauthorized $400 charge with no resolution offered, and a Shopify integration specifically reported as failing on a weekly basis with multi-day support-resolution times. Neither of these is a vague dissatisfaction — they're concrete, specific problems that should factor directly into any decision to commit to the required 6-month minimum subscription term. My honest read: if Kommo's CRM-native messaging architecture is genuinely what you need, and your lead-qualification workflow is scripted rather than open-ended, this is a differentiated, credible option — but get explicit, written billing terms confirmed, and stress-test any Shopify integration you plan to rely on before committing past the free trial.
